## Active

### D-201 — the realm adapts a service, so the CRUD scaffolding went

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · active_

The realm is named @feasibleone/blong-realm and exposes the blong namespace, as asked, so the usual
folder equals package equals namespace rule is deliberately broken here: the package says realm, the
namespace says blong. The kopi template supplies tables, models, CRUD seeds and CRUD tests for an
entity it owns; this realm owns no data and adapts the semantic-log cluster service, so meta/model,
meta/type, adapter/db, adapter/dbTest, the server and browser CRUD test groups, the Playwright CRUD
spec, the template README and CHANGELOG were removed. What remains is the entry points, the subject
namespace on both platforms, the error map and the RBAC seed.

### D-207 — The refusal spec asserts why, not just that something was refused

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · active_

A screenshot cannot tell a 403 from a 404, so the realm passed its refusal test while its entire API
was missing from the gateway. The spec now also asserts that the collected browser errors name the
refusal and the method.

### D-206 — The realm's portal menu lives in portalConfigGet

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · active_

Removed the realm component that held the portal menu list, because its handler was referenced
nowhere: the menu has one source now, the portalConfigGet handler the framework actually calls. Its
entries carry the page method ids, so a renamed page is a menu entry that opens nothing rather than
a silently absent one.

### D-222 — The six reads are conversions, not handlers calling exec

> _2026-09-18 · core/blong-realm · active_

The realm had a `semlogGet` library that called the port own `exec` from each of six handlers. It is
now the framework two conversion seams: one `<method>RequestSend` per read, which the port loop runs
before the call and hands to the adapter `exec` (the same seam the jsonrpc and mle codecs use -
their `send` builds a `{path, responseType, json}` descriptor for exactly this), and one
`responseReceive` that hands the body on and refuses to flatten a refusal. The six method handlers
are gone: a handler for a method would be called *with the descriptor* and would have to re-enter
`exec`, which is the detour this removes. Consequences, all verified by the tap flow and the browser
spec: the realm contains no HTTP code at all; the path of each read lives in a file named after the
method it serves; and because no handler names a method any more, `gateway/blong/` is the ONLY
declaration of the six (its validation files register the route and the parameters) - so a new
method needs both its `<method>RequestSend` and its gateway file, and nothing else. The port still
imports the group: without it the conversions are not attached and `exec` would receive raw params.

### D-243 — The flow page bounds its own areas instead of relying on the shell

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-realm · active_

The page fills the tab (height: 100%) and gives the execution list and the diagram a bounded box
each, both overflow: auto, with the list capped at half the page. Before this, the page grew with
its content (a long list is as tall as the process has been up, a sequence diagram as tall as the
flow was busy) and .blong-app's overflow: hidden clipped everything past the fold with no scrollbar
anywhere: measured 20187px of page in a 670px panel. The alternative fix - making the tab panel
itself scroll (Portal.css) - was written first and reverted: it fixes the class of bug for every
page, but it makes the page's scroll position part of whatever a spec captures afterwards, and three
realm baselines went run-dependent.

### D-250 — A cell that is masked in a capture is given a fixed box

> _2026-09-22 · core/blong-realm · active_

The digest page masks its When cell (a wall clock cannot be pinned) and the flow page masks its
Execution cell (a minted ULID cannot be pinned), and both now render that value inside a span with a
fixed width. The reason is that masking paints over a value and changes nothing about its layout: an
ISO timestamp is as wide as its digits and a ULID as wide as its Crockford letters, so a masked cell
whose width varies moves every column after it and the comparison fails on pixels no reviewer can
see (F-228). Rejected: masking a wider region (the shift moves with it), and capturing a fixed-size
slice of the page (the page is the artifact). The cost is a fixed column width on the page, which is
what a table whose value cannot be pinned should have.

## Superseded

### D-202 — the realm is a port plus a namespace orchestrator

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · superseded_

The six reads live in adapter/service/ behind a port named service, and the blong namespace belongs
to orchestrator/blong.ts, which forwards to that port by name. The port name is load bearing: it is
the destination the orchestrator names. The port extends adapter.http, but the client fetches
directly, because the base adapter reads its URL from the http slice and crashes on its own config
hook when that slice is missing. Neither alternative works: the shared subject orchestrator turns
blong.flow.find into a query for a table that does not exist, and a port named after the namespace
404s as an unknown remote port.

the port is named semlog and reads go through the adapter exec

Superseded by `D-219`.

Superseded: the nested http slice, the fetch client and the adapter is own URL default are gone.

### D-219 — The semantic-log reader is a library on a semlog port, reached through exec

> _2026-09-18 · core/blong-realm · superseded_

The realm reads the cluster service through a port named `semlog` (folder `adapter/semlog/`, group
`blong.semlog`), not `service`: a port called `service` names every adapter in every realm that has
one, and the framework names an instantiation after its role. The URL moved from the nested `http`
key to the base adapter own `url` key - the slice it actually reads - and each read went through the
base adapter `exec` instead of `fetch`, with `$meta` forwarded, so the deployment URL, the TLS
settings and the timeouts are the port own and an adapter-level interceptor can see the call. The
reader was a `library` (file `semlogGet.ts`, default export), because a plain module in a
handler-group folder is what the loader reports as "a generic source code was put in a handler group
folder" - an ERROR in the log that the template page then listed as a row. The orchestrator imports
no group: it declares the namespace and reaches the port through `destination`.

Superseded by `D-222`, which replaced the library and the per-method handlers with one `RequestSend`
conversion per method plus a single `responseReceive`.
